definition: Efforts to protect and improve the health of everyone in a place by changing shared conditions, not just treating individuals.
The science and practice of preventing disease and promoting health in whole populations.
A group of people who share something, such as a neighborhood, city, or age group.
The average number of years a newborn is expected to live if current conditions stay the same.
The conditions where people are born, live, learn, work, and play that shape health.
Everyone has a fair chance to be as healthy as possible; some groups need more support to get there.
In Riverton: life expectancy in the best-off neighborhood minus the worst-off neighborhood.
How often something happens compared with the size of the group, such as cases per 1,000 people.
Six linked steps by which a germ spreads: germ, reservoir, portal of exit, mode of transmission, portal of entry, susceptible host.
Ongoing, systematic collection and review of health data to spot problems and outbreaks.
Rules for who counts as a case of an outbreak: person, place, time, and clinical features.
A histogram of the number of new cases by date or time of illness onset.
The proportion of people at risk who become ill: cases divided by people exposed.
The attack rate in exposed people divided by the attack rate in unexposed people.
When a third factor linked to both the exposure and the illness makes an exposure look related (or unrelated) to illness.
The share of true cases that a definition or test correctly catches.
The share of non-cases that a definition or test correctly excludes.
A series of steps for community decisions: define the problem with data, identify who is affected, listen, consider evidence-based options, weigh equity and trade-offs, decide, evaluate.
Anyone affected by a decision or able to influence it.
False or misleading information, often shared without bad intent.
A person the community already trusts, who helps accurate health information be believed.
Actions that change the causes of poor health, such as housing, income, and clean air.
Actions that respond after harm has happened, such as emergency care.
Primary stops problems before they start, secondary finds them early, and tertiary limits harm from existing problems.
